caption:
Hours before planned bombings, Trump cancels US strikes on Iran. A diplomatic breakthrough or a tactical pause?

President Donald Trump cancelled planned U.S. military strikes and bombings against Iran on Thursday, citing breakthroughs in high-level negotiations with Tehran's leadership.

The decision came just hours before the attacks were expected to take place, following more than three months of conflict that has killed thousands of people, primarily in Iran and Lebanon.

Trump stated that the agreement had been approved by a broad coalition of regional powers, including Israel, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Turkey, Pakistan, Bahrain, Kuwait, Jordan, and Egypt.

Despite the cancellation of strikes, the US President confirmed that the naval blockade against Iran will remain in full force until the final transaction is signed.

Earlier in the day, Trump had threatened to hit Iran 'very hard' and expressed interest in taking over the oil infrastructure hub, Kharg Island.

Global oil prices fell sharply and stocks rose following the announcement of the cancellation of the military strikes.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has called on both sides to redouble efforts toward a peaceful, comprehensive, and durable agreement.

While progress has been reported, some sources indicate that specific details, such as the release of frozen Iranian funds, have not yet been discussed in detail.
